Please provide an MRP to make this easier to test and fix:
- A small Godot project which reproduces the issue, with no unnecessary files included. Be sure to not include the `.godot` folder in the archive (but keep `project.godot`).
- Having an MRP is very important for contributors to be able to reproduce the bug in the same way that you are experiencing it. When testing a potential fix for the issue, contributors will use the MRP to validate that the fix is working as intended.
- Drag and drop a ZIP archive to upload it (max 10 MB). **Do not select another field until the project is done uploading.**
- **Note for C# users:** If your issue is *not* C#-specific, please upload a minimal reproduction project written in GDScript. This will make it easier for contributors to reproduce the issue locally as not everyone has a .NET setup available. 

Can you also test on 4.4.1 to see if this is an old bug or a new regression?

[particlebug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22210506/particlebug.zip)

Check it out.

Load the game, move camera up and down via W/S on your keyboard. The particle effects slowly move up. Move your camera down so the particles are off-screen. Wait a few seconds, then scroll up. You'll see a noticeable gap in the particles, because for some reason it's showing you old particles of its previous location when you last saw it before updating (presumably).

I tried on 4.4.1, no difference.

I suppose it's more likely that old particles just aren't being cleaned up and kind of just sit there until they're in the viewport again.

Hello, I am having a problem related to GPUParticles3D in my project which might be related to this issue.

In my project, when the player character  `is_on_floor()` becomes `true`  a particle system is played once:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ce0ef469-f2cf-436b-bc8c-6846f6c0f461

This particle system is does not feature any movement in the Y axis, and its `local_coord` property is set to `false`. However, when the player jumps again right after landing (and the camera follows its movement) the particles move "downwards" even though they are following the global coordinate system:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d34e58f9-d24f-4f9f-a0b3-3dbb6bc2a535

If this example is relevant to the issue, I can try and create a MRP that covers this specific case.
